instructors.bio:
Chris spent years in advertising and writing before jumping into standup four years ago. Since then, he’s been performing all over California (and soon across the country) and is currently building his first one-hour special.

He remembers exactly what it’s like to be new, overthink every word, and hold onto the mic stand for dear life. Chris focuses on structure, joke-writing, and how to keep things playful instead of paralyzing.

Focus: Joke writing, marketing & branding
Skill Level: Beginner to intermediate

Sommer has spent years on stages in Chicago and Los Angeles, both performing and directing. As an acting coach and comic, she knows how to pull honest, surprising moments out of people who swear they’re “not performers.” Her superpower: helping you feel safe enough to be weird—and precise enough to be funny.

She’s directed and taught performers at every level and loves watching “I could never do that” turn into “oh my god, I just did that.”

Focus: Performance, stage presence, multi-discipline studies (i.e. acting & comedy)
Skill Level: Beginner to advanced

Mike Muratore has earned the moniker of “The Serial Killer of Comedy” with his brand of raw, in-your-face, no holds barred comedy. His act has been honed in the worst venues possible for comedy over the past 20 years. Playing terrible venues has turned Mike into one of the best comedians performing today. Will you be offended? Yes. Will you be scared? Probably. Will you emerge better? Definitely.

Focus: Crowd work, roasting, getting booked
Skill Level: Intermediate to advanced

Jim is a native of Illinois. Not Chicago, the part with all the corn and soybeans. He fell in love with comedy at an early age, he laughed way too hard at cartoons, The Carol Burnett Show, SNL and SCTV, and his life was set on its course by seeing This Is Spinal Tap. While living in Chicago, he devoted his time to theatre and improv, taking classes at Second City, IO, and The Annoyance Theatre. In Los Angeles, he continued improvising and added standup comedy to his resume. Oh yeah, he’s done some TV, too. You can see him in Weeds, The Wizards of Waverly Place, The Thundermans, Black Monday with Regina Hall, Ryan Murphy productions HOLLYWOOD and Monster: The Jeffrey Dahmer Story, and most recently, The Conners, with Laurie Metcalf.

Focus: Acting, writing, one-person shows, character development
Skill Level: Beginner to advanced

Alice performs standup all over LA, as well as tours in Chicago, San Francisco, and New York. She has headlined at Flappers Comedy Club and Tao Comedy Studio. Alice also produces standup shows, including Cabana Comedy in Los Angeles and Live, Laugh, Pup in Idyllwild. In addition to standup comedy, Alice is an actor and writer. Her solo show Inconceivable recently won the Best Newcomer Award for Solofest 2025 and will be running at the Hollywood Fringe Fest in June 2026. Alice currently teaches acting and standup comedy at Idyllwild Arts Academy.
